action_criteria.expected_evidence: Serum anti-GluN1 positive (1:256); sodium 127 mmol/L (moderate hyponatraemia) with potassium 3.3 mmol/L; thyroid function, thyroid antibodies and other neuronal antibodies negative; beta-hCG negative
action_criteria.label: Obtain the reviewed serum work-up, including a cell-based IgG anti-GluN1 assay that must be interpreted with CSF rather than alone
action_criteria.rationale: Excludes metabolic, endocrine (including postpartum thyroid), toxic and infective mimics, excludes pregnancy, and gives the serum anti-GluN1 result, which is read with the CSF assay.

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Bilateral hippocampal FLAIR hyperintensity without restricted diffusion, haemorrhage or enhancement; no structural lesion or venous sinus abnormality
action_criteria.label: Obtain contrast-enhanced brain MRI to exclude HSV encephalitis, structural lesions and overlapping demyelination; a normal MRI does not exclude anti-NMDAR encephalitis
action_criteria.rationale: Excludes HSV encephalitis, structural lesions and overlapping demyelination before LP; it is normal in most patients and does not confirm the diagnosis.

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Lymphocytic pleocytosis (52 cells/uL), protein 79 mg/dL, 5 CSF-restricted oligoclonal bands and IgG index 1.01; HSV PCR negative; CSF IgG anti-GluN1 positive (1:64) on cell-based assay
action_criteria.label: Analyze CSF for cells, protein and glucose, OCB/IgG index, HSV PCR and a cell-based IgG anti-GluN1 assay interpreted in parallel with serum
action_criteria.rationale: CSF anti-GluN1 IgG on a cell-based assay is the decisive test for definite disease, and HSV PCR addresses the can't-miss infectious mimic.

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Extreme delta brush and one left temporal electrographic seizure on a slow background
action_criteria.label: Obtain EEG for encephalopathic and epileptiform abnormalities, explicitly assessing for extreme delta brush
action_criteria.rationale: Staring spells with posturing, a convulsive seizure and dyskinesias need an EEG to separate seizures from movements; an abnormal EEG supports the diagnosis.

action_criteria.label: Screen for an ovarian teratoma with pelvic and abdominal ultrasound
action_criteria.rationale: Women of reproductive age carry the highest teratoma risk, and she has a right ovarian cyst known from pregnancy; tumour removal is part of first-line treatment.

action_criteria.label: Escalate to continuous EEG monitoring for seizure burden and non-convulsive seizures
action_criteria.rationale: An electrographic seizure on a routine EEG with staring spells and confusion: continuous EEG measures the seizure burden.

action_criteria.rationale: Sodium 127 mmol/L needs serum and urine osmolality to confirm SIADH before fluid restriction.

prohibited_recommendations: Do not give haloperidol or other high-potency D2 antagonists for agitation: patients with anti-NMDAR encephalitis are prone to severe extrapyramidal and neuroleptic-malignant-like reactions.
Do not delay immunotherapy while waiting for the anti-NMDAR antibody result when clinical probability is high: antibody turnaround can take 1-2 weeks and delay worsens outcome.
Do not attribute the presentation to a primary psychiatric disorder while seizures, dyskinesias, autonomic instability, an abnormal EEG or CSF inflammation remain unexplained.
Do not perform lumbar puncture without prior imaging in a patient with altered consciousness, focal signs, or new seizures: exclude mass effect first.
Do not interpret a negative serum anti-NMDAR antibody as ruling out the disease; the CSF assay is the gold standard and may be positive when serum is negative.
required_recommendations: Start IV aciclovir 10 mg/kg every 8 hours at presentation, and stop it once CSF HSV PCR is negative and the antibody diagnosis is established; repeat the PCR on a second CSF sample if the first LP was within 72 hours of onset and HSV encephalitis remains plausible.

Start first-line immunotherapy without waiting for the antibody result once infection is reasonably excluded: IV methylprednisolone 1 g daily for 5 days with IVIG 0.4 g/kg/day for 5 days (2 g/kg total) or plasma exchange (5 to 7 exchanges).
Arrange prompt surgical removal of the right ovarian teratoma (laparoscopic, ovary-sparing where feasible) as part of first-line treatment, with gynaecology.
Treat seizures with an antiseizure medication such as levetiracetam or lacosamide; avoid valproate in a woman able to become pregnant; seizures respond mainly to immunotherapy.
Monitor with continuous EEG for non-convulsive seizures while consciousness fluctuates or seizures persist.

Admit to a neurology ward or step-down unit with seizure precautions and continuous cardiac monitoring; transfer to the ICU if consciousness falls, hypoventilation appears or the autonomic instability (heart rate 124 bpm, blood pressure 158/96 mmHg, diaphoresis) worsens.

If there is no meaningful clinical improvement 10 to 14 days after first-line therapy, escalate to rituximab (375 mg/m² weekly for 4 doses or 1 g twice 2 weeks apart, after hepatitis B screening) and/or cyclophosphamide; discuss fertility preservation before cyclophosphamide.
Treat agitation and insomnia with benzodiazepines (lorazepam) first.
Treat the moderate hyponatraemia (127 mmol/L) as SIADH: fluid restriction, correcting by no more than 10 mmol/L in 24 hours; give IV aciclovir in isotonic saline rather than free water.
Replace potassium (3.3 mmol/L) and recheck it during high-dose corticosteroids.
Neurology-led care with psychiatry for behavioural management; gynaecology for the teratoma.

avoided_actions.rationale: Transthoracic echo is not indicated for anti-NMDAR encephalitis; it adds cost without informing diagnosis or management unless a discrete cardiac concern (e.g., new murmur, embolic stroke) coexists.
EMG/NCS plays no role in the diagnostic workup of anti-NMDAR encephalitis; it neither confirms the antibody-mediated CNS process nor distinguishes among the differential diagnoses.
Amyloid PET targets Alzheimer pathology and contributes no information to the diagnosis or treatment of autoimmune encephalitis in a young patient with subacute neuropsychiatric symptoms.

DaTscan evaluates nigrostriatal dopaminergic function and has no role in autoimmune encephalitis; the orofacial dyskinesias of anti-NMDAR encephalitis are antibody-mediated, not presynaptic dopaminergic.

differential.key_features: CSF HSV PCR negative on an LP about 2 weeks after onset; MRI hippocampal signal symmetric, without haemorrhage or restricted diffusion; CSF anti-GluN1 positive.

differential.diagnosis: Other antibody-mediated encephalitis (anti-LGI1, CASPR2, GABA-B or AMPA receptor)
differential.key_features: Serum neuronal-surface panel negative (LGI1, CASPR2, GABA-B, AMPA) and onconeural antibodies negative; the hyponatraemia does not make LGI1 encephalitis likely with CSF anti-GluN1 positive.

differential.diagnosis: Postpartum psychosis or other primary psychiatric disorder
differential.key_features: Onset 14 months after delivery, well beyond the early postpartum weeks when postpartum psychosis begins; seizures, orofacial dyskinesias, autonomic instability, extreme delta brush and CSF pleocytosis with oligoclonal bands are not explained by a psychiatric disorder.

differential.diagnosis: Postpartum thyroid dysfunction (thyroiditis or Hashimoto encephalopathy)
differential.key_features: TSH 2.1 mIU/L and free T4 normal, anti-TPO 11 IU/mL; a well-characterised neuronal antibody is present.

differential.diagnosis: Drug-induced psychosis or neuroleptic malignant syndrome
differential.key_features: No substance or antipsychotic exposure; urine drug screen negative; CK only 196 U/L with dyskinesias and seizures.

key_clinical_evidence: Subacute onset over 2 weeks, after a febrile upper respiratory illness, of insomnia, guilt and paranoid delusions, perseverative speech, focal and generalized seizures, orofacial dyskinesias with choreoathetosis and autonomic instability: at least five of the six Graus 2016 groups.
CSF IgG anti-GluN1 positive (titre 1:64) on cell-based assay: definite anti-NMDAR encephalitis (Graus 2016); serum positive 1:256 is read with the CSF.

MRI shows bilateral hippocampal FLAIR signal without restricted diffusion, haemorrhage or enhancement; MRI is normal or non-specific in about two thirds and excludes structural causes, while the negative CSF HSV PCR excludes HSV encephalitis.
EEG shows extreme delta brush and a left temporal electrographic seizure; extreme delta brush, when present, supports but does not establish the diagnosis.
Pelvic ultrasound shows a 5.8 cm right ovarian mature cystic teratoma at the site of the cyst known from pregnancy: its removal is part of first-line treatment.
Onset 14 months after delivery argues against postpartum psychosis.
Earlier immunotherapy and tumour removal are associated with better outcome (Titulaer 2013).

red_herrings.correct_interpretation: A viral-like prodrome precedes about 70% of anti-NMDAR encephalitis; it does not establish viral encephalitis, which CSF PCR addresses.
red_herrings.data_point: Febrile upper respiratory infection 3 weeks earlier (fever 38.9, sore throat, cervical lymphadenopathy) preceding the neuropsychiatric syndrome.
red_herrings.intended_effect: Suggests a primary viral encephalitis (HSV) or post-viral psychosis; tempts the agent to commit to empiric antiviral therapy without pursuing autoimmune workup.

red_herrings.correct_interpretation: Postpartum psychosis begins in the first weeks after delivery, not at 14 months; seizures, dyskinesias, dysautonomia, an abnormal EEG and CSF pleocytosis require exclusion of autoimmune encephalitis before a psychiatric diagnosis is accepted.
red_herrings.data_point: Insomnia, guilt about being 'a bad mother' and paranoid delusions in a mother of a 14-month-old, which her husband attributes to postpartum depression or psychosis.
red_herrings.intended_effect: Anchors the agent on a primary psychiatric diagnosis (first-episode psychosis, brief psychotic disorder) and delays neurologic workup.

red_herrings.correct_interpretation: Hyponatraemia occurs in anti-NMDAR encephalitis but is more typical of anti-LGI1 encephalitis; it needs its own work-up and correction and does not point away from the diagnosis.
red_herrings.intended_effect: Tempts the agent toward a primary metabolic-encephalopathy framing (SIADH from another cause, dehydration, polydipsia) instead of recognizing SIADH as a known complication of NMDAR-E.

contraindications: Haloperidol and other high-potency D2 antagonists (class warning): severe extrapyramidal and neuroleptic-malignant-like reactions are reported in anti-NMDAR encephalitis.
interactions: Methylprednisolone: lowers potassium further (current potassium 3.3 mmol/L) and raises glucose; replace potassium and monitor.
Aciclovir IV with fluid restriction for hyponatraemia: aciclovir needs adequate hydration to avoid crystal nephropathy; give it in isotonic saline and monitor creatinine.
IVIG: can lower measured sodium (pseudohyponatraemia from the protein load) and carries thrombotic and renal risks; interpret sodium with serum osmolality.
Cetirizine + lorazepam + levetiracetam: additive sedation; monitor consciousness and breathing.

general.summary: No interaction prevents the planned therapy. Steroids worsen the low potassium; aciclovir needs isotonic fluid despite the fluid restriction; IVIG can lower the measured sodium.
warnings: Screen for hepatitis B (HBsAg, anti-HBc) before any rituximab dose.
Cyclophosphamide is teratogenic and gonadotoxic: effective contraception and fertility counselling are needed.

anti-NMDA receptor encephalitis diagnosi.query: anti-NMDA receptor encephalitis diagnosis and treatment

results.finding: Definite anti-NMDAR encephalitis requires one or more of six major symptom groups and IgG anti-GluN1 antibodies, with CSF testing included; probable disease requires four groups (or three with a teratoma) of rapid onset plus an abnormal EEG or CSF pleocytosis or oligoclonal bands.
results.source: Graus F et al. Lancet Neurol 2016;15:391-404

results.finding: All patients had antibodies in CSF, whereas about 14% were negative in serum; CSF titres related more closely to outcome than serum titres.
results.source: Gresa-Arribas N et al. Lancet Neurol 2014;13:167-177

results.finding: 38% had a tumour, mostly ovarian teratoma; 53% improved within 4 weeks of first-line immunotherapy or tumour removal; second-line rituximab or cyclophosphamide after first-line failure was associated with better outcome; 81% had mRS 0-2 at 24 months.
results.source: Titulaer MJ et al. Lancet Neurol 2013;12:157-165

results.finding: Extreme delta brush was found in 7 of 23 adults with anti-NMDAR encephalitis and was associated with a more prolonged illness.

anti-NMDA receptor encephalitis diagnosi.summary: Published criteria and cohort data on anti-NMDA receptor encephalitis: definite diagnosis rests on CSF IgG anti-GluN1 antibodies; first-line immunotherapy and tumour removal are followed by second-line agents when there is no response.

patient.history_present_illness: A 29-year-old right-handed woman, 14 months post-partum, was brought to the emergency department by her husband who describes a 2-week deterioration with a presentation that he initially attributed to postpartum depression, before recognizing it was something far more serious. The patient had been in her normal state of health until approximately 3 weeks ago when she developed a significant upper respiratory infection with documented fever (38.9), sore throat, and cervical lymphadenopathy lasting 7 days. After apparent recovery, she began developing insomnia about 2 weeks ago, which her husband initially attributed to the baby disrupting sleep, but he noticed she was not sleeping even when the baby was with her mother. Within days her personality changed dramatically: she became withdrawn, expressed guilt about being 'a bad mother,' and then progressed to frank paranoid delusions — accusing her husband of having an affair and eventually 'being replaced by a robot.' Simultaneously she developed repetitive uncontrollable facial movements that she was embarrassed about and tried to hide. Her husband witnessed two brief episodes of staring with arm posturing over the following week. On the day of presentation she had a 3-minute generalized tonic-clonic seizure during which her husband called 911. On arrival she is agitated, confused, and has obvious uncontrolled facial movements. Her husband specifically asks the team if this could be related to an ovarian tumor he read about in the context of 'brain inflammation.' The patient's last menstrual period was 6 weeks ago (resumed post-partum). She breastfed until her daughter was 12 months old and has since weaned. She has a history of a right ovarian cyst noted during her pregnancy ultrasound that was followed and showed no significant interval change on repeat ultrasound at 34 weeks gestation.

neurological_exam.additional: Autonomic instability: HR 124, BP 158/96, temp 37.9, diaphoresis. No meningismus.
neurological_exam.cranial_nerves: Pupils 4mm bilaterally, reactive. Continuous involuntary perioral and tongue movements. Mild hypersalivation.
neurological_exam.mental_status: Alert, intermittently agitated and confused. Not oriented. Continuous orofacial dyskinesias — lip-smacking, jaw-clenching, tongue thrusting. Perseverative speech patterns. Post-ictal confusion noted at beginning of evaluation but improving.
neurological_exam.motor: Distal bilateral choreoathetosis. Full strength on brief cooperative exam. Bilateral upper extremity posturing intermittently.
